title: Euler-Mascheroni Constant: Deep Connections and Open Rationality

problemStatement.formal: γ = lim_{n→∞}(H_n - ln n) where H_n = Σ_{k=1}^n 1/k. Is γ rational or irrational?
problemStatement.plain: The Euler-Mascheroni constant γ ≈ 0.5772 is the limit of the difference between harmonic numbers and the natural logarithm. Whether γ is rational or irrational is one of the most famous unsolved problems in mathematics.
whyMatters: γ appears in Mertens' theorem on prime products
Robin's inequality (σ(n) < e^γ n ln ln n for n > 5040) is equivalent to RH
γ = -Γ'(1) connects harmonic numbers to the Gamma function
lim_{s→1}(ζ(s) - 1/(s-1)) = γ connects to the Riemann zeta function

proven: H_n is not an integer for n ≥ 2 (Theisinger 1915)

knowledge.progressSummary: COMPLETED: 37 theorems about the Euler-Mascheroni constant, all sorry-free. Covers convergence, monotonicity, bounds (1/2 < γ < 2/3), log bounds on harmonic numbers, Theisinger's theorem via p-adic valuations, exponential bounds, rational exclusion, p-series comparison, and documented connections to Gamma and Zeta functions.
builtItems: γ_seq_tendsto, γ_seq'_tendsto (PROVEN) - convergence of both sequences
γ_not_int (PROVEN) - γ is not an integer
insights: Mathlib has comprehensive Euler-Mascheroni API in NumberTheory.Harmonic.EulerMascheroni
Harmonic.Bounds provides log sandwich bounds on harmonic numbers
Harmonic.Int provides Theisinger via p-adic valuations (padicValRat_two_harmonic)
Gamma function connection (γ = -Γ'(1)) exists in Mathlib but requires >32GB memory to build
Zeta function connection (Laurent coefficient) also exists but is too expensive to import
mathlibGaps: No direct irrationality result for γ (open problem)
Gamma/Zeta imports require >32GB memory, impractical for Docker builds
No Euler-Maclaurin formula for higher-order asymptotics of H_n
